The response should mention that each specialist plays a defined role: surgical oncologists assess resectability and operative planning; medical oncologists direct systemic therapy; radiation oncologists evaluate indications for radiotherapy; gastroenterologists manage biliary and gastrointestinal complications; geneticists perform germline and somatic testing; nutritionists address malnutrition and enzyme replacement; and palliative care teams optimize symptom management and psychosocial support
The response should mention that clear patient-centered communication is essential
The response should mention that multidisciplinary tumor board meetings where all team members review imaging, pathology, and clinical status can help to reach consensus on the care plan
The response should mention to identify a central coordinator such as a lead physician, nurse navigator, or case manager
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're concerned about emergency situations. What should we be prepared for?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that patients with pancreatic cancer are at high risk for several acute emergencies due to tumor progression, treatment effects, and comorbidities

The response should mention that biliary obstruction, gastric outlet obstruction, VTE, severe pain crises, febrile neutropenia, metabolic derangements, bowel obstruction, and spinal cord compression are the most common emergencies in pancreatic cancer
The response should mention that biliary obstruction typically presents with yellowing of the skin (jaundice), dark urine, and itchiness (pruritus)
The response should mention that Gastric outlet obstruction manifests as persistent vomiting, inability to tolerate oral intake, and abdominal distension

The response should mention that blood clots (such as venous thromboembolism) are common in pancreatic cancer, with symptoms including sudden leg swelling, pain, shortness of breath, or chest pain; pulmonary embolism is a leading cause of death after cancer itself

The response should mention that fever in patients with low white blood cells (febrile neutropenia) is a life-threatening complication of chemotherapy, characterized by fever and signs of infection in the context of neutropenia

The response should mention that lab abnormalities such as high calcium (hypercalcemia causing confusion, weakness, constipation) and low sodium (hyponatremia; causing confusion, seizures) can occur in pancreatic cancer
The response should mention that bowel obstruction presents with abdominal pain, vomiting, and constipation
The response should mention that spinal cord compression may cause new-onset weakness, sensory changes, or loss of bowel/bladder control
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My father has pancreatic cancer and is experiencing hearing changes. Is this related to treatment?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that hearing changes in patients with pancreatic cancer can be related to treatment
The response should mention that platinum-based chemotherapy (such as cisplatin) is well-known to cause hearing loss (ototoxicity)
The response should mention that the risk of hearing loss increases with cumulative doses and patient age
The response should mention that other therapies, including aminoglycoside antibiotics, loop diuretics, and radiation to the head/neck, can also contribute to hearing loss
The response should mention that hearing changes may result from direct cancer involvement, such as metastases affecting cranial nerves or brain, but this is uncommon in pancreatic cancer
The response should mention that referral for audiologic evaluation is advised
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My mother has pancreatic cancer and we're considering proton therapy. What is this and when is it used?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that proton therapy is a form of external beam radiation that uses protons rather than photons to deliver highly conformal radiation doses to tumors

The response should mention that physical properties of protons allow for precise dose deposition with minimal exit dose, which can reduce radiation exposure to adjacent organs such as the stomach, duodenum, and bowel

The response should mention that proton therapy is a safe and feasible option for select patients with locally advanced or recurrent pancreatic cancer, especially when minimizing toxicity to surrounding organs is critical
The response should mention that the use of proton therapy should be individualized based on tumor location, patient anatomy, and multidisciplinary evaluation
The response should mention that proton therapy is often used in combination with chemotherapy (such as gemcitabine) as part of concurrent chemoradiation protocols
The response should mention that proton therapy can be used for locally advanced, unresectable, or recurrent disease
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and is worried about the cost of medications. What assistance programs are available?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that Assistance programs available to help with the cost of medications for a patient with pancreatic cancer include several federal, state, manufacturer, and independent charity options

The response should mention that for those who qualify, Medicaid offers comprehensive prescription drug coverage with minimal co-payments, and is the most effective public program for low-income patients

The response should mention that Many brand-name cancer drugs offer manufacturer-sponsored assistance programs that provide free or discounted medications to eligible uninsured or underinsured patients, usually requiring proof of financial hardship and doctor certification

The response should mention that Independent nonprofits like HealthWell and PAN Foundation offer co-pay and premium assistance to insured patients with incomes below 400--500% of the federal poverty level
The response should mention that accessing assistance programs can be complex, with disparities among non-English speakers and some ethnic groups
The response should mention that Financial navigators and online tools (e.g., NeedyMeds, RxAssist) can help
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My husband has pancreatic cancer and his oncologist mentioned maintenance therapy. What does this mean?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that maintenance therapy refers to a treatment strategy used after initial therapy has controlled the disease, with the goal of prolonging survival and maintaining quality of life
The response should mention that maintenance therapy typically involves either de-escalating to less toxic agents for eligible patients
The response should mention that the decision to initiate maintenance therapy should be individualized, considering disease response, cumulative toxicities, patient preference, and goals of care
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're dealing with treatment-related anxiety. What resources are available?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that resources such as psychotherapy, psychoeducation, supportive therapy, and integrative modalities are available to support patients with treatment-related anxiety

The response should mention that Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) is the first-line intervention for treatment-related anxiety in patients with pancreatic cancer, as recommended by the American Society of Clinical Oncology, due to its strong evidence for reducing anxiety symptoms in cancer populations

The response should mention that mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs), including mindfulness-based stress reduction, are strongly recommended by the American Society of Clinical Oncology and the Society for Integrative Oncology

The response should mention that pharmacologic therapy may be considered for patients with severe anxiety or those who do not respond to first-line psychological interventions, though the evidence base is weaker and this is a secondary option per the American Society of Clinical Oncology
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My father has pancreatic cancer and is considering cryotherapy. What is this treatment?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that cryotherapy (also called cryoablation) is a minimally invasive locoregional treatment that destroys tumor tissue by freezing it, typically using probes inserted through the skin (percutaneously) or intraoperatively under imaging guidance

The response should mention that in pancreatic cancer, cryotherapy is not a standard first-line therapy but is considered for patients with unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic disease who are not candidates for surgical resection or have failed systemic therapy
The response should mention that its primary role is palliative, aiming to reduce tumor burden, alleviate pain, and potentially improve quality of life and local disease control
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My mother has pancreatic cancer and we want to understand more about tumor markers beyond CA 19-9. What others are there?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) and other tumor markers such as carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), cancer antigen 125 (CA125) can be used for diagnosis, prognosis, or monitoring in patients with pancreatic cancer
The response should mention that CEA and CA125 are the most widely used supplementary markers
The response should mention that CEA is elevated in 30--60% of pancreatic cancer cases and is particularly useful in Lewis-negative patients who do not secrete CA19-9

The response should mention that both CEA and CA125 have demonstrated value for diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring, especially when CA19-9 is not informative. CA125, when combined with CA19-9, improves diagnostic accuracy and is associated with tumor burden and metastatic disease
The response should mention that DUPAN-2 and CA242 are carbohydrate antigens that can complement CA19-9, especially in patients with genetic variants affecting CA19-9 synthesis
The response should mention that emerging markers such as LAMC2, POSTN are not yet standard in routine clinical practice
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and is experiencing hand-foot syndrome from chemotherapy. How is this managed?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that hand-foot syndrome (HFS) is a common, non-life-threatening but quality-of-life-impacting cutaneous toxicity of chemotherapeutic agents, particularly capecitabine and other fluoropyrimidines used in pancreatic cancer

The response should mention that HFS presents with redness (erythema), changes in sensation (dysesthesia), pain, cracking, and peeling (desquamation) of the palms and soles, and can significantly impair daily function, especially in elderly patients
The response should mention that prevention strategies include celecoxib, urea cream

The response should mention that cooling procedures, such as frozen gloves or socks applied during taxane infusions, may prevent or reduce HFS severity and are recommended by the Oncology Nursing Society for taxane-based regimens
The response should mention that prevention strategies such as Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) and lactic acid have not shown consistent benefit for prevention or treatment of HFS in randomized trials
The response should mention that omeprazole (a proton pump inhibitor) and tipiracil (a thymidine phosphorylase inhibitor) may have prophylactic effects, but these are not yet standard practice
The response should mention that management of established HFS includes topical urea and corticosteroids
The response should mention that Photobiomodulation (low-level laser therapy) has shown promise as an adjunct for pain and symptom control

The response should mention that for grade ≥2 HFS, interruption or reduction of chemotherapy dose is the mainstay of management, as continued exposure may worsen symptoms and necessitate treatment discontinuation
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My husband has pancreatic cancer and we're considering treatment at a cancer center versus community oncology. What's the difference?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that Cancer Centers include NCI-designated comprehensive cancer centers and academic medical centers
The response should mention that cancer centers are often located in major cities, which can mean longer travel times, more complex scheduling, and larger, busier environments
The response should mention community oncology clinics, on the other hand, are typically more accessible and closer to home
The response should mention that in some cases initial treatment planning can be done at a cancer center, follow-up care can be done at a community center closer to home
The response should mention that the best choice depends on the specific treatment needed, the patient's health, and the support systems are available

The response should mention that receiving pancreatic cancer treatment at a specialized cancer center is associated with greater use of modern combination therapies, improved access to clinical trials, and superior survival outcomes compared to community oncology practices

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and is worried about intimacy during treatment. How do we address this?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that concerns about intimacy during treatment for a loved one with pancreatic cancer are common
The response should mention that changes in intimacy include decreased desire, arousal disorders, pain, erectile dysfunction, altered body image, and emotional distress
The response should mention that interventions to address intimacy concerns include psychosocial, psychosexual, and couples-based therapies
The response should mention that referral options include medical sexologists, psycho-sexologists, social worker, and psychologist
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My father has pancreatic cancer and his doctors mentioned radiofrequency ablation. What is this?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is a minimally invasive locoregional therapy that uses thermal energy to induce coagulative necrosis and cell death within tumor tissue

The response should mention that in pancreatic cancer, RFA is most commonly delivered via endoscopic ultrasound guidance (EUS-RFA), allowing precise targeting of the tumor while minimizing injury to surrounding structures
The response should mention that radiofrequency ablation is used in pancreatic cancer primarily for unresectable or inoperable tumors as a palliative or adjunctive therapy
The response should mention that RFA is not a substitute for surgery or systemic therapy in resectable disease
The response should mention that the side effects of RFA are usually mild, with most adverse events being mild and self-limited, such as transient abdominal pain or mild pancreatitis
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My mother has pancreatic cancer and we're trying to manage her medications. She's on so many pills - is this normal?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that it is normal for patients with pancreatic cancer to be on multiple medications to manage both the cancer and treatment-related side effects
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and is considering yoga during treatment. Is this safe and beneficial?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that yoga is generally safe for people with cancer, including those undergoing treatment for pancreatic cancer

The response should mention that yoga may help reduce cancer-related fatigue, anxiety, and depression, and improve quality of life and emotional well-being during and after treatment, though effects are typically small to moderate and the certainty of evidence is low to moderate
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My husband has pancreatic cancer and we're worried about long-term side effects of treatment. What should we expect?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that long-term side effects in patients treated for pancreatic cancer are common
The response should mention that long term side effects are due cumulative impact of surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, and the underlying disease

The response should mention that the most frequent chronic effects include fatigue, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (especially with oxaliplatin or taxanes), chronic pain, sexual dysfunction, cognitive changes ("chemo brain"), metabolic derangements (such as diabetes and osteoporosis), and nutritional deficiencies due to pancreatic exocrine insufficiency
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and wants to donate to pancreatic cancer research. What organizations should we consider?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that nonprofit organizations are vital for supporting innovative research in pancreatic cancer

The response should mention that donations to nonprofit organizations can support research, clinical trials, and patient support initiatives, addressing critical gaps in funding and accelerating progress in pancreatic cancer care

The response should mention that organizations to consider include Pancreatic Cancer Action Network (PanCAN), American Association for Cancer Research (AACR), the National Cancer Institute (NCI), and the National Pancreas Foundation (NPF)

questions.question_text: My father has pancreatic cancer and is experiencing vision changes. Could this be treatment-related?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that vision changes in a patient with pancreatic cancer can be related to cancer treatment

The response should mention that chemotherapy can cause vision changes (ocular toxicity). For example, gemcitabine and 5-fluorouracil, have been associated with retinal findings including cotton-wool spots and other visual disturbances
The response should mention that ocular metastases may cause vision changes
The response should mention that paraneoplastic syndromes may cause vision changes
The response should mention that an eye evaluation is recommended for new vision changes during cancer therapy to distinguish between treatment-related toxicity, disease progression, and other causes
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My mother has pancreatic cancer and we're considering telehealth appointments. Are these as effective as in-person visits?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that telehealth appointments are generally as effective as in-person visits for many aspects of care for patients with pancreatic cancer

The response should mention that Telehealth offers benefits, including reduced travel burden, lower costs, decreased infection risk, and improved access expertise, which is especially valuable for patients distant from high-volume centers
The response should mention that telehealth may be less suitable for initial diagnosis, physical examinations, or sensitive discussions (e.g., new diagnosis, end-of-life care)

The response should mention that limitations of telehealth include challenges with physical examination, technology barriers, and occasional concerns about reduced personal connection or quality of interaction

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and is worried about hair loss from chemotherapy. What can we expect?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that hair loss from chemotherapy is a common and distressing side effect in patients undergoing treatment for pancreatic cancer
The response should mention that the estimated incidence of hair loss with chemotherapy is up to 65% depending on the regimen used

The response should mention that the pattern is typically diffuse, nonscarring alopecia (anagen effluvium), beginning within weeks of starting cytotoxic agents such as FOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine-based regimens
The response should mention that the severity and risk is higher with multi-agent and taxane-containing protocols, and female patients also are at increased risk

The response should mention that most cases are reversible, with regrowth expected within 3--6 months after cessation of chemotherapy, but persistent or permanent alopecia can occur, especially after repeated or high-dose regimens
The response should mention that eyebrow and eyelash loss may also be seen
The response should mention that scalp cooling devices can reduce the risk and severity of hair loss, with success rates of 50--80% in clinical studies
The response should mention that topical minoxidil may aid regrowth post-chemotherapy, though evidence for prevention is limited
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My husband has pancreatic cancer and his oncologist mentioned oligometastatic disease. What does this mean?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that oligometastatic disease in the context of pancreatic cancer refers to a clinical state where the cancer has spread beyond the pancreas but the number and sites of metastases are limited, typically involving a single organ (most often liver or lung) and a small number of lesions, commonly defined as ≤3 to ≤5 metastases

The response should mention that patients with oligometastatic pancreatic cancer may be considered for more aggressive multimodal therapy, including systemic chemotherapy followed by local treatments such as surgery, ablation, or stereotactic radiotherapy, if there is good response to initial therapy
The response should mention that patients with oligometastatic disease have the potential for improved prognosis compared to widespread metastatic disease
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're dealing with treatment delays due to low blood counts. Is this common?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that it is common for patients with pancreatic cancer to experience treatment delays due to low blood counts
The response should mention that these delays are often necessary to ensure patient safety
The response should mention that dose reductions may help prevent severe neutropenia and treatment suspension, but must be weighed against potential reductions in treatment efficacy
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My father has pancreatic cancer and is considering hyperthermia treatment. What is this?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that hyperthermia treatment is a locoregional or whole-body therapy in which tumor tissue is heated to 39--43°C to enhance the cytotoxic effects of chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy

The response should mention that in pancreatic cancer, hyperthermia is most commonly used as an adjunct to standard chemoradiotherapy for patients with locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic disease, particularly when conventional therapies have limited efficacy or are refractory
The response should mention that hyperthermia can be delivered regionally (deep regional hyperthermia), intraoperatively, or as whole-body hyperthermia
The response should mention that adding hyperthermia to chemoradiotherapy may improve overall response rates and median survival compared to standard therapy alone, with acceptable safety profiles

The response should mention that the quality of evidence is limited, and hyperthermia remains investigational, with ongoing trials evaluating its efficacy and optimal integration into multimodal treatment regimens
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My mother has pancreatic cancer and we want to understand more about her genetic testing results. Who can help interpret these?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that board-certified genetic counselors, medical geneticists, and oncologists with expertise in hereditary cancer syndromes can help interpret genetic testing results for a patient with pancreatic cancer

The response should mention that board-certified genetic counselors, medical geneticists, and oncologists can help determine clinical significance of identified variants, discuss implications for surveillance, prevention, and treatment, and provide guidance for at-risk family members

The response should mention that pathogenic variants in genes such as BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, ATM, CDKN2A, and others, which may influence both therapeutic decisions and recommendations for family screening
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and is experiencing taste changes. How can we manage this?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that taste changes are common in patients with pancreatic cancer undergoing chemotherapy, with prevalence estimates ranging from 56--76% depending on treatment modality, and can significantly impair nutritional intake, food enjoyment, and quality of life
The response should mention that improved oral hygiene and active swallowing exercises may also promote taste recovery

The response should mention that a referral to a registered dietitian is recommended for tailored nutritional strategies, as taste changes often lead to reduced appetite, altered food preferences, and risk of malnutrition
The response should mention that dietitians can assist with food texture modification, flavor enhancement, and strategies to maintain adequate caloric and protein intake

The response should mention that pharmacological and supplement-based interventions have been explored with mixed results. Further research is needed to establish standardized, effective interventions
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist or dietician

questions.question_text: My husband has pancreatic cancer and we're considering exercise during treatment. What's safe and beneficial?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that The American Society of Clinical Oncology recommends that patients with pancreatic cancer undergoing treatment engage in aerobic and resistance exercise, as both are safe and beneficial for patients with pancreatic cancer during chemotherapy, chemoradiotherapy, or neoadjuvant therapy
The response should mention that physical activity should be tailored to individual capacity and comorbidities

The response should mention that aerobic exercise (such as walking, cycling, or swimming) and resistance training (using weights or resistance bands) improve cardiorespiratory fitness, physical function, and reduce symptoms like fatigue and mood disturbances
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're worried about the progression of the disease. What signs should we watch for?

rubric_items.description: The response should mention that signs and symptoms that indicate disease progression in pancreatic cancer include new or worsening jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, pruritus, abdominal pain (especially if persistent or increasing), back pain, weight loss, anorexia, fatigue, nausea/vomiting, constipation, diarrhea, new or worsening diabetes, bloating, belching, and cachexia

The response should mention that alarm symptoms such as gastrointestinal bleeding or rapidly declining performance status should also be recognized as potential indicators of advanced disease or complications
The response should mention that close monitoring of symptoms is essential for timely intervention and supportive care
The response should mention that early integration of supportive care is recommended to optimize quality of life and address complications as they arise
The response should recommend that the user discuss this case with an oncologist
